title: Use strong unique passwords
summary: A unique password is used for only one account. A password manager can create and remember long passwords so one leak does not unlock many accounts.
introduction: A unique password is used for only one account. A password manager can create and remember long passwords so one leak does not unlock many accounts. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A unique password is used for only one account. A password manager can create and remember long passwords so one leak does not unlock many accounts.

blocks.code:
Account A: its own long password
Account B: a different long password
Password manager: stores them in its protected vault
blocks.title: Use strong unique passwords

blocks.text: Reusing one password would connect the risk of both accounts. Never put real passwords into this tutorial.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why a different password for each account helps.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A password written as an example in public is not a password to use.
For more detail later, use this [Cybersecurity Fundamentals further reading](https://www.cisa.gov/secure-our-world).
